abertura: You get three minutes before anyone asks you anything. Most people spend them saying what the company does.
Mark the three statements that are true of those three minutes.

itens.t: Their job is to make the buyer want to ask a question.
itens.porque: Yes. Three minutes that end in silence failed, however complete they were.

itens.t: They should cover everything the company does.
itens.porque: No. Everything the company does is what a website is for. This is a room with three people and a shortlist.

itens.t: What you leave out matters as much as what you say.
itens.porque: Yes. What you leave out is what tells them where you think the value is.

itens.t: Detail builds credibility, so more of it is better.
itens.porque: No — detail with no question behind it reads as not knowing what matters.

itens.t: The one thing only you can say belongs in them.
itens.porque: Yes. Anyone can read the numbers. Only you can say why you would do this deal.

itens.t: If you go over, they will stop you.
itens.porque: No. They will let you run over and count it as the answer to a question they did not have to ask.

sec1.rationale: Nobody stops you at three minutes; they stop listening, which is worse because you cannot see it. Three minutes that end with a question from them is the whole objective.

nota.texto: Everything from the last three lessons arrives here at once: saying it back, asking for it again, and keeping the form while you think about something else. Nothing new is introduced today.

doc.texto:
Who is in the room
Diane Whitfield (corporate development), Mark (finance) and Peter (adviser). They have spoken to two other companies in the region.

What they already know
Roughly what you do, roughly your size, and the numbers you sent on Thursday. Nothing about how you work.

What they came to decide
Whether to open a conversation about a minority position — not whether to buy the company.

What you have
Three minutes at the top of the call, and then their questions.

abertura: Where does each of these belong?
opcoes: in the answers, if they ask

itens.t: What the company does, in one sentence.
itens.ok: in the three minutes
itens.porque: In the three minutes — and in ONE sentence. If it takes three, the rest of the time is already spent.

itens.t: Why this conversation is worth their time.
itens.ok: in the three minutes
itens.porque: In the three minutes. It is the only line in the list that answers the question they actually have.

itens.t: The revenue split, in detail, by service line.
itens.ok: in the answers, if they ask
itens.porque: In the answers. They asked for the split by email; giving it again out loud spends the time twice.

itens.t: What you would want out of a minority position.
itens.ok: in the three minutes
itens.porque: In the three minutes. It is the offer question from the first email, and it is the one only you can answer.

itens.t: The full list of your enterprise clients.
itens.ok: in the answers, if they ask
itens.porque: In the answers, if they ask. A client list read aloud is the fastest way to lose a room.

itens.t: What you think their board will decide.
itens.ok: not in this meeting
itens.porque: Not in this meeting. Guessing at their board in front of them turns a conversation into a negotiation.

nota.titulo: The one people always put in the wrong place
nota.texto: What you would want out of a minority position feels like an answer to a question they have not asked. It is not: they said in their own call that this is what they came to decide. Saying it first is what makes the three minutes theirs.

nota.titulo: Four of them are for questions you did not expect
nota.texto: None of the six is about the company. They are all about staying in the conversation — which is the thing that was missing in the meeting that did not go your way.

abertura: They will ask how many of your delivery team have already delivered in English -- delivered, not attended calls. Suppose the honest answer is: four people.
Mark the three answers that keep the conversation.

itens.t: "Four have delivered in English. Everyone else has worked with English-speaking clients, but not led."
itens.porque: Yes. The number, and then what surrounds it — the honest figure with the context that makes it readable.

itens.t: "All of them can work in English."
itens.porque: No. It is not true, and the first place it will be checked is due diligence.

itens.t: "Four today. If we go ahead, that is the number I would be hiring against."
itens.porque: Yes. It turns a weakness into a plan, which is what a buyer is listening for.

itens.t: "That would not be a problem for us."
itens.porque: No — it answers a question they did not ask and avoids the one they did.

itens.t: "Four -- and I would rather tell you that now than in due diligence."
itens.porque: Yes. Saying it now is worth more than the four; it tells them what you do with bad news.

itens.t: "It depends on what you mean by delivered."
itens.porque: No. Redefining the word is what people do when the answer is worse than four.

sec4.rationale: The three that work all start with the number. Two of the three that do not are the comfortable answers, and both of them get checked in due diligence, where being wrong costs far more than being small.

nota.texto: They told each other, in their own call, that a no changes the price and the timeline and not whether they do the deal. The number is not the risk. Discovering it later is.

sec5.titulo: The question you did not expect
abertura: One of the three is the move that keeps you in the conversation.

itens.t: They ask something you did not prepare for.
alts: That is a fair question -- the way we handle it is...
That is not really my area.
I would have to check that.
itens.ok: That is a fair question -- the way we handle it is...

itens.t: You are not sure which of two things they are asking about.
alts: Before I answer, can I check what you mean by delivery?
I think you mean delivery.
Can you repeat the question?
itens.ok: Before I answer, can I check what you mean by delivery?

itens.t: You genuinely do not have what they are asking for.
alts: We are working on it.
That is a good point.
We do not have that today. What we do have is...
itens.ok: We do not have that today. What we do have is...

itens.t: They asked two things and you have only answered one.
alts: Let me come back to your first point.
Was that everything?
I think I answered that.
itens.ok: Let me come back to your first point.

itens.t: They spoke fast and you lost the end of the question.
alts: Sorry?
Sorry, could you say the second part again?
I did not understand the question.
itens.ok: Sorry, could you say the second part again?

nota.titulo: None of these is about English
nota.texto: A person who runs a company in Portuguese does all five of these every day without noticing. The only thing that is new is that they have to come out in another language, at the speed of the question.

sec6.titulo: Your three minutes, written down first
abertura: Complete the skeleton. Five sentences, and the whole three minutes fits in them.
Write it about your own company -- this is the one activity in the block where the invented version would be worth less.
itens: {We are|80px} a data and AI company, and what we actually do is solve one problem for our clients.
{The reason this conversation is worth your time is|320px} that we already do at scale what you are buying elsewhere.
{What I would want out of it is|210px} a partner, and not an exit.
{We do not have|130px} everything in English today, and I would rather say that now.
{What I would ask you for is|190px} one hour with your delivery people, before anybody talks about structure.

nota.titulo: This is what you will say with nothing on the screen
nota.texto: Five sentences is three minutes at a normal speaking pace. If it takes you longer than that to read them out loud, the sentences are too long — and long sentences are also where the verb endings go missing.

cl4.prompt: Three of these keep the conversation. Which three?

itens.t: "Four have delivered in English. Everyone else has worked with English-speaking clients, but not led."
itens.porque: Yes. The number first, the context second, and nothing softened.

itens.t: "All of them can work in English."
itens.porque: No. Untrue, and it will be checked.

itens.t: "Four today -- and that is the number I would be hiring against."
itens.porque: Yes. It says what you would do about it, which is the part they can act on.

itens.t: "That would not be a problem for us."
itens.porque: No. It avoids the number, and avoiding a number is itself an answer.

itens.t: "Four, and I would rather tell you now than in due diligence."
itens.porque: Yes. It puts the bad news before due diligence does, which is the whole move.

cl4.rationale: All three that work start with the number. The two that do not are the comfortable answers -- and both get checked later, where being wrong costs more than being small.
